entries.title: Set up your own email domain yourself
entries.summary: **Settings > Domains**, for the organization and for each event, walks you through the From address, the DNS records and verification, with clear statuses and errors. Copy the instructions for Slack or Teams, or email them to your IT contact straight from the page. Sessionboard checks the records every 10 minutes and emails you when they verify, and the organization's page lists every event's address and status.

enable.path: Ask support to enable Custom Sending Domain for the organization; then Settings → Domains → add your From address and the DNS records it shows

where.path: Org Settings → Domains; Event Settings → Domains

entries.use_case: Email from the customer's own domain is the #1 deliverability and trust fix, and it used to need support. Now the organizer or their IT contact does it, with Slack/Teams-ready instructions, auto-verification every 10 minutes and an org-wide status page.

cs_action.note: Gated by the org flag custom_sending_domain (Admin → Features & Enhancements). Turn it on for the customer, then point them at Settings → Domains. Staff skip the flag check, so a CSM can also run the setup for them.

internal.staff_path: Admin → org → Features & Enhancements → Custom Sending Domain; site domains stay staff-only on the same Domains page.
internal.when_to_bring_up: Deliverability complaints, onboarding, any customer not yet on a custom sending domain, SPF/DMARC questions from IT.
internal.who_should_get_it: Every customer still sending from a Sessionboard address; prioritise those with open deliverability tickets.
internal.gotchas: Per-event addresses are listed on the organization's page with their status.

entries.title: Evaluation plans: Replace cleans up the whole round
entries.summary: The **Replace not-yet-reviewed** and **Replace all** options now remove assignments on submissions that no longer match the rule and take those submissions out of the round, so the round count matches the filter; the preview and confirmation show how many submissions leave. Reviewed assignments are still kept with Replace not-yet-reviewed, and entered scores are never deleted.

where.path: Event → Evaluations → plan → Assignments → Assign reviewers → Replace not-yet-reviewed / Replace all

entries.use_case: Program chairs who re-track or re-categorise submissions after a round was assigned no longer end up with a round whose count disagrees with its filter, or with reviewers holding abstracts that moved out of their track.

cs_action.note: Replace all now removes assignments on submissions that fell out of the filter, including reviewed ones. Customers who use Replace all mid-round should read the confirmation counts; walk any medical/scientific customer through it before their next assignment pass.

internal.when_to_bring_up: A customer says the round count does not match the filter, or reviewers still see submissions that were moved to another track.
internal.who_should_get_it: Everyone running round-based evaluations; especially multi-track scientific programs that correct categories after assignment.
internal.gotchas: Scores are never deleted even when an assignment is removed. Replace not-yet-reviewed keeps any assignment with review activity.

entries.title: Status filters include custom statuses
entries.summary: In evaluation plan filters and Automations, **Status is Pending** now also matches submissions in a custom status under Pending such as **In Review**, so an Assign reviewers automation no longer skips them with a filter mismatch.

where.path: Event → Automations → When card → Status filter; Evaluations → plan → submission filters

entries.use_case: Customers with custom statuses (In Review, Shortlisted…) under a standard one no longer need a filter per custom status, and automations stop silently skipping submissions that sit in one.

cs_action.note: Any customer whose Assign reviewers automation showed "filter mismatch" in Delivery history for sessions in a custom status: this is the fix. Tell them.

internal.when_to_bring_up: Delivery history shows skipped runs with "filter mismatch"; a customer asks why In Review sessions were not assigned.
internal.who_should_get_it: Customers using custom statuses together with Automations or evaluation plan filters.
internal.gotchas: To match a single custom status, pick that status in the filter instead of its parent.

entries.title: Automations: Contact created trigger
entries.summary: People automations can fire once for each new contact, narrowed by where they came from: added by your team, imported, from an integration, or from a form or portal.

enable.path: Event → Automations → New automation → People → When: Contact created → Created through

entries.use_case: Welcome emails and task creation the moment a speaker or contact lands on the event — and only for the sources you choose, so people who filled in their own details are not emailed twice.

cs_action.note: A good demo moment for any customer importing speaker lists or syncing from a registration platform.

internal.when_to_bring_up: Onboarding, "how do I welcome new speakers automatically", any customer doing imports or integrations into an event.
internal.who_should_get_it: Every customer using Automations; especially those importing or syncing contacts.
internal.gotchas: Contacts created through the Public API, and contacts created at the organization level without an event, do not fire this trigger.

entries.title: Automations: email your team, and react only to the person's own changes
entries.summary: A Send email step can also email event team members and team tags, or only them. Field-change triggers gain **Only when the submitter makes the change** (sessions) and **Only when the contact makes the change** (people), so edits by your team, imports and integrations don't fire them.

enable.path: Event → Automations → Send email step → Team members; When card → Only when the submitter / contact makes the change

where.path: Event → Automations → Send email step and When card

entries.use_case: "Tell me when a speaker updates their own bio" is now one automation: it emails the team, and it ignores the team's own edits and imports so it does not fire on every bulk update.

cs_action.note: Customers who turned off a field-change automation because it fired on imports can turn it back on with the new checkbox.

internal.when_to_bring_up: A customer asks to be notified of speaker self-service edits, or complains an automation fires during imports.
internal.gotchas: Each email needs at least one recipient. A team tag resolves when the email sends, so it reaches whoever holds the tag at that moment.

entries.title: Custom success page on Awards and Interest Forms
entries.summary: Write the message applicants and speakers read after they submit, in place of the default "What's next?" list.

enable.path: Awards → form builder → Success page tab; CRM → Interest Forms → form → Success page message

where.path: Awards form builder → Success page; Interest Form wizard → Details

entries.use_case: Awards and CRM customers can tell applicants exactly what happens next — when finalists are announced, what to prepare — instead of a generic list, which cuts the "what now?" emails after a submission.

cs_action.note: Available to anyone with Awards or Speaker CRM; nothing to enable beyond the add-on itself.

internal.when_to_bring_up: Awards program setup, Interest Form setup, any customer asking to change the confirmation text.
internal.gotchas: Leave the editor empty to keep the default list. Confirmation number, PDF download and Return to Portal still appear.

entries.title: Require secure links on URL fields
entries.summary: A URL field can save every `http://` link as `https://`, in the admin, submission forms and Awards applications.

enable.path: Settings → Fields → URL field → Require secure links (https://)

where.path: Org or Event Settings → Fields → a URL field

entries.use_case: Speaker websites and LinkedIn links pasted as http:// break on HTTPS-only program sites and embeds; this normalises them at save time with no cleanup pass.

internal.when_to_bring_up: Mixed-content warnings on a program site or embed; a customer cleaning up speaker URLs.
internal.who_should_get_it: Everyone publishing speaker or session links.
internal.gotchas: Off for new fields by default. Links already saved keep their address until someone edits them.

entries.title: Content galleries: My list goes home with the visitor
entries.summary: **Add to calendar** downloads saved sessions as a calendar file and **Email me my list** sends every saved item with its link. Recordings can be added to a gallery straight from the Media Hub with **Add to gallery**.

where.path: Published gallery → My list; Marketing → Media library → recording → Add to gallery

entries.use_case: A visitor who saved sessions in a gallery can take the list to their calendar or inbox, which is the moment a content library turns into attendance and a captured email.

internal.when_to_bring_up: Content Galleries pilots; customers asking how a gallery drives registrations or captures leads.
internal.who_should_get_it: Customers in the Content Galleries preview.
internal.gotchas: Add to calendar appears only once a saved item has a start time. Embargoed details stay hidden in the email; sending is rate-limited.

entries.title: Agenda embeds show any session field
entries.summary: The **Agenda** field tab lists every standard and custom session field, up to nine in the session pop-up.

enable.path: Embeds are enabled per event by support; then Event → Embeds → embed → Fields → Agenda tab

where.path: Event → Embeds → an agenda embed → Fields → Agenda

entries.use_case: Customers embedding the agenda on their own site can show CE credits, room, level or any custom field in the session pop-up without a feed and custom code.

internal.when_to_bring_up: A customer asks to show a custom field (credits, level, track colour) on their embedded agenda.
internal.who_should_get_it: Customers with Embeds enabled on an event.
internal.gotchas: Nine fields maximum in the pop-up; JSON and XML feeds are not limited. Ticking Starts At or Ends At also prints the time on the grid card.

entries.title: Evaluation plans: clearer assigning
entries.summary: The Assign button counts the evaluations it will create, **Done** on the Assignments step is now **Close without assigning**, and leaving with an unassigned change asks first. The same applies to Awards rounds.

where.path: Event → Evaluations → plan → Assignments step; Awards → round → Assign reviewers

entries.use_case: Chairs stopped losing assignment rules by clicking Done thinking it saved; the button now says what it does and the count makes the blast radius obvious before it is committed.

internal.when_to_bring_up: A customer reports "my assignments disappeared" after configuring a rule.
internal.who_should_get_it: Everyone running evaluations or Awards rounds.

entries.title: Interest Forms: Speakers Only forms assign without a session
entries.summary: Assigning a Speakers Only submission adds its speakers to the event's contacts without creating a session.

where.path: CRM → Pipeline → submission → Assign to event

entries.use_case: Speakers Only forms are the CRM's general intake; assigning one to an event used to create an empty session the team then had to delete.

internal.when_to_bring_up: A CRM customer complains about empty sessions appearing after assigning interest-form submissions.
internal.who_should_get_it: Speaker CRM customers using Speakers Only forms.
